target_customer: Philanthropic funders (GiveWell, Open Philanthropy and others) who pay for cash incentives given to caregivers in northern Nigeria
problem: Low routine childhood vaccination coverage in northwest Nigeria, partly because transport costs and weak demand keep caregivers from completing the vaccine schedule.
business_model: Nonprofit funded by grants and donations; pays small conditional cash transfers to caregivers after verified vaccinations
product_category: Conditional cash transfer program for childhood immunization (global health nonprofit)

founders.name: Svetha Janumpalli
founders.background_notes: Researched conditional cash transfers with the Center for Effective Global Action before starting the organization (company history page). Education and prior employers not found in opened sources.

founders.name: Pratyush Agarwal
founders.background_notes: Company history page says he joined as co-founder during the YC phase in 2016. Background not found.

founders.name: Patrick Stadler
founders.background_notes: Named by the company history page as a co-founder who joined during the YC phase. Not listed on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Core work is operational: paying caregivers by verified clinic visit and tracking vaccinations across many clinics in northern Nigeria. Hard parts were data verification and field logistics, not novel technology.

defensibility.rationale: Nonprofit with funder trust and a later randomized trial, which is hard to copy quickly, though the idea of paying for vaccination was open to anyone.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found of any incumbent copying or buying the program; it kept growing as a GiveWell top charity (GiveWell lookback, 2025).

market_need_then: North West Nigeria had very low routine vaccination coverage and frequent measles outbreaks; a 2016 pilot proposal targeted transport cost as a barrier (GiveWell hosted pilot proposal, Oct 2016).

branding.domain_note: Uses newincentives.org (nonprofit domain); no acquisition story found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain evidence-driven language such as the tagline Cash transfers that save lives

branding.community_and_virality: Recognized by charity evaluators and funders such as GiveWell, Founders Pledge and Charity Navigator per its site; no evidence of merch or fan community.

brand_strength.rationale: Brand rests on evaluator endorsements and results rather than the name; the name is generic. No press about the brand itself was found.

pivots.from: Conditional cash transfers for preventing mother-to-child HIV transmission and facility delivery
pivots.why: After reassessing evidence on neonatal mortality and finding fewer HIV-positive pregnant women than expected (company history page)

outcome_analysis: New Incentives pivoted during its 2016 YC batch from HIV and delivery incentives to vaccination incentives, ran a randomized trial that found higher coverage, and became a GiveWell top charity from 2020. Funding came as philanthropic grants that grew from about 5.9 million dollars in 2017 to larger multi-million grants in 2022 and 2023. No shutdown or controversy was found.
notes: GiveWell says over 120 million dollars directed to New Incentives for 2020 to 2026 (July 2025 lookback), so the rounds list is partial. The 2011 seed funder is Unorthodox Philanthropy per the company but a Lampert Family Foundation per GiveWell search summary (conflict). Nonprofit, so no valuations. No competitor sourced near the 2016 batch found; list left empty. Outcome search found no shutdown or layoffs.
